To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
immunosuppressants affect the expression of several proteins in the rat kidney, which are involved in calcium homeostasis, cytoskeletal structure, mitochondrial function and cell metabolism.

immunosuppressants and sirolimus induce changes in protein expression in the kidney, which are related to changes in urine metabolites, which are indicative of changes in kidney physiology and metabolism.
immunosuppressants and sirolimus induce changes in the renal proteome that explain the observed changes in urine metabolites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the investigation of drug-induced nephrotoxic effects.
the identification of biomarker candidates that may be used for early diagnosis of nephrotoxic effects.
a novel proteo-metabolic approach that may be used to study the effects of drugs in the kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
immunosuppressants and immunosuppressing regimens have a significant impact on renal metabolism.
cyclosporine induces metabolic changes in the rat, which are reflected in urine, that can be explained by changes in protein expression.

cyclosporine-induced protein expression changes were associated with and qualified changes in the urinary metabolite pattern, whereas tacrolimus-induced protein expression changes did not explain urinary metabolite pattern changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the observed metabolic changes in urine are the result of changes in protein expression in the kidney.
cyclosporine and sirolimus induce a complex set of changes in protein expression in the kidney, which are reflected in changes in urine metabolic patterns.
cyclosporine and tacrolimus affect different pathways in the kidney, which may be responsible for different nephrotoxic effects of these drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
proteo-metabolic profiling is a powerful tool to identify the underlying mechanisms of drug-induced nephrotoxic effects.

urine (1) H-NMR metabolite pattern changes can be explained by changes in protein expression and that proteo-metabolomics may be a powerful tool for studying the effects of drugs on renal physiology and pathology.
proteo-metabolomic studies may be used to identify and explain changes in protein expression and to identify potential biomarkers for nephrotoxic drug-induced renal damage.
